title: Tennis ball falling at 30 m s⁻¹
caption: At 30 m s⁻¹ the same ball's drag, 0.92 N, is bigger than its 0.59 N weight (ratio 1.6): drag grows as v², so the idealisation that worked at 5 m s⁻¹ fails completely here, and the ball slows down.
alt: Free-body diagram of a falling tennis ball: weight 0.59 N down and drag 0.92 N up.
description: The ball is shown as a box. Its weight, mg = 0.06 × 9.81 = 0.59 N, acts straight down.
Drag acts upward, against the motion: ½ρC_dAv² = ½ × 1.2 × 0.5 × 0.0034 × 30² = 0.92 N, drawn to the same scale.
Drag ÷ weight = 1.56; the net force is 0.33 N upward.
notes: drag ÷ weight ≈ 1.6: drag cannot be neglected

claims.name: drag ÷ weight = 1.56 from ½ρC_dAv² and mg
